title: Mock 3 · Numbers Drill
blurb: Light numericals in every chapter (PV, PEG, CAPM, duration, fees, Sharpe, LTCG) mixed with must-know PMS rules.

questions.q: An investor is certain to receive ₹110 one year from today. If the risk-free rate is 10%, the present value is:
hints: Wrong: subtracts 10% of 110 instead of discounting.
Wrong: ignores time value of money.

questions.q: An Indian investor holds US stocks. If the rupee strengthens (appreciates) against the dollar, her returns in rupee terms will:
questions.explanation: Appreciation of the home currency reduces returns from foreign assets; the workbook example shows INR returns may decline if the rupee strengthens.
hints: Wrong: depreciation of the rupee would increase returns.
Correct: rupee appreciation reduces INR returns.
Wrong: currency moves affect returns on foreign assets.

questions.q: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, a 'retail individual investor' is one who applies in an IPO/FPO for a value of not more than:
questions.explanation: A retail individual investor applies or bids for specified securities for a value of not more than ₹2 lakh.
hints: Wrong: ₹10 lakh is the PMLA cash threshold.

questions.q: A stock has a P/E of 30 and expected EPS growth of 20%. Its PEG ratio and the usual interpretation are:
questions.explanation: PEG = 30 / 20 = 1.5. A PEG greater than 1 can indicate the stock is overvalued.
hints: Wrong: growth divided by P/E, inverted.

questions.q: Using CAPM, with a risk-free rate of 6%, beta of 1.2 and expected market return of 12%, the cost of equity is:
hints: Wrong: multiplies market return by beta without subtracting Rf.
Wrong: this is only the risk premium part.
Wrong: adds the full market return to the premium.

questions.q: In the event of liquidation of a company, equity shareholders are paid:
options: Last, after all debts and liabilities are settled
questions.explanation: Equity is a residual claim: holders are last to be paid after all debts and liabilities.
hints: Wrong: lenders rank ahead of equity.
Wrong: ownership does not give priority.

questions.q: A bond has a modified duration of 6. If market yields rise by 0.50%, its price will change by approximately:
questions.explanation: % change in price = - Modified Duration x change in yield = -6 x 0.005 = -3%.
hints: Wrong: prices fall when yields rise.
Wrong: ignores the size of the yield change.

questions.q: A trader with no underlying position buys a one-month futures contract at ₹102. At expiry the asset trades at ₹98. Ignoring costs, the trader's result per unit is:
questions.explanation: Long futures at 102, settled at 98: loss = 102 - 98 = ₹4. A view-based trade without an underlying position is speculation.
hints: Wrong: a long position loses when prices fall.
Wrong: compares with an assumed spot of 100.

questions.q: A REIT that invests in real estate loans and mortgage-backed securities and earns interest income is a:
questions.explanation: Mortgage REITs invest in real estate loans and MBS and earn income from interest.
hints: Wrong: equity REITs own properties and earn rent.
Wrong: hybrid REITs earn both rent and interest.

questions.q: If a portfolio manager aggregates purchases for several clients for economy of scale, the inter se allocation must be done:
options: Pro rata at the weighted average price of the day's transactions
At the discretion of the dealer
First come first served at actual prices
In favour of the largest client
questions.explanation: Inter se allocation shall be done on a pro rata basis at the weighted average price of the day's transactions, with no open position in allocation.
hints: Correct: pro rata at weighted average price.
Wrong: no discretion; fairness is mandated.

questions.q: A portfolio manager is required to preserve its books of account and records for:
questions.explanation: The PM must preserve books of account and other records for the preceding five accounting years.
hints: Wrong: 8 years relates to F&O loss carry forward.

questions.q: Which of the following is a portfolio manager permitted to do?
options: Invest client funds in a portfolio managed by another portfolio manager
Participate in securities lending with written client authorisation
Charge distribution fees when investing in MF direct plans
Deploy client funds in bill discounting
questions.explanation: The PM may, subject to written authorisation by the client, participate in securities lending. The other actions are expressly prohibited.
hints: Correct: allowed with written client authorisation.
Wrong: no distribution fee on direct plans.
Wrong: bill discounting and badla are prohibited.

questions.q: A client's average daily AUM for the year is ₹80 lakh. The maximum operating expenses (excluding brokerage) the PM may charge over and above its fee is:
A PMS charges a 20% performance fee above a 10% hurdle rate. On ₹1 crore, the portfolio earns 15% in a year (ignore other fees). The performance fee is:
questions.explanation: Fee applies only on the 5% excess: 5% x ₹1 crore = ₹5 lakh; 20% of ₹5 lakh = ₹1,00,000.
hints: Wrong: 20% of the entire ₹15 lakh gain.
Wrong: 20% of the ₹10 lakh hurdle amount.

questions.q: For new clients on-boarded on or after which date must portfolio managers ensure compliance with the MITC (Most Important Terms and Conditions) requirement?
questions.explanation: MITC applies to new clients on-boarded on or after October 01, 2024; existing clients were to be informed by January 01, 2025.
hints: Wrong: this was the deadline for existing clients.
Wrong: this is the ADR Regulation 22A date.
Wrong: this is the PMS guidelines circular date.

questions.q: On the workbook's sample risk profiling questionnaire, an investor scores 22. She falls in the category:
questions.explanation: Bands: 25-30 Aggressive, 19-24 Moderate, 13-18 Conservative, below 13 Risk-averse. 22 is Moderate (balanced allocation).

questions.q: Compared with Strategic Asset Allocation, Tactical Asset Allocation typically has:
options: Lower risk and less frequent rebalancing
Higher risk and more frequent adjustments
A fixed asset mix for decades
questions.explanation: TAA is short-term and active, with more frequent adjustments and higher risk due to market timing.
hints: Correct: TAA is active and riskier.

questions.q: Under SEBI's performance benchmarking framework, each investment approach must be tagged to:
questions.explanation: Each investment approach shall be tagged to one and only one strategy among equity, debt, hybrid and multi-asset.
hints: Wrong: tagging to a strategy is required.

questions.q: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, a resident individual may remit up to how much per financial year for permissible transactions?
questions.explanation: LRS allows resident individuals, including minors, to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year. It began in 2004 at USD 25,000.

questions.q: A portfolio returned 14% with a standard deviation of 16% when the risk-free rate was 6%. The Sharpe ratio is:
hints: Wrong: return divided by SD without subtracting Rf.
Wrong: excess return not divided by risk.

questions.q: A PMS earns a pre-tax return of 15% and the investor's applicable tax rate is 20%. The post-tax return is:
questions.explanation: Post-tax return = Pre-tax return x (1 - tax rate) = 15% x 0.80 = 12%.
hints: Wrong: this is the tax amount.

questions.q: A resident investor's total equity LTCG for the year (all from PMS, no other gains) is ₹3,00,000. Ignoring surcharge and cess, the tax payable is:
questions.explanation: LTCG up to ₹1.25 lakh is exempt; taxable = 3,00,000 - 1,25,000 = 1,75,000; tax at 12.5% = ₹21,875.

questions.q: A resident investor receives total dividends of ₹8,000 from a company in FY 2025-26. According to the workbook, TDS on these dividends is:
options: Not deducted, since the threshold from FY 2025-26 is ₹10,000
questions.explanation: Companies deduct TDS at 10% on dividends exceeding ₹5,000; this limit has been increased to ₹10,000 from FY 2025-26. ₹8,000 is below the threshold.
hints: Wrong: the dividend is below the new threshold.
Wrong: 20% is the NRI dividend TDS mentioned.
Wrong: TDS is not on the excess only.

questions.q: Under Schedule C of the insider trading regulations, pre-cleared trades must be executed by the designated person within:
questions.explanation: The code of conduct shall specify a timeframe not exceeding seven trading days for executing pre-cleared trades, failing which fresh pre-clearance is needed.
hints: Correct: not more than 7 trading days.
Wrong: 6 months is the minimum contra-trade period.

questions.q: Under the PaRRVA framework operationalised by SEBI in April 2026, which entity is recognised as the verifying agency?
questions.explanation: Care Ratings Limited is recognised as the PaRRVA verifying agency; NSE functions as the PaRRVA Data Centre.
hints: Wrong: APMI prescribes benchmarks and valuation norms.
Wrong: NSE is the PaRRVA Data Centre.
